answer.rationale: Write-path degradation is confined to the primary region; failover to the secondary region removes traffic from the affected path while preserving writes (no rollback of the compliance-mandated security patch, no capacity lag). Settlement peak means we need continuity of writes, which failover provides. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) addresses dashboard load on the primary, but the current symptom is write-path latency, not report load. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect against partner outages, not internal primary-region degradation. Capacity adds risk of provisioning lag during peak. Failover is the single intervention that directly isolates the degraded region without sacrificing the security patch or the settlement writes.
